The paper studies a robust optimal stopping problem with respect to a set of mutually singular probabilities.
The optimal stopping problem can be interpreted as a zero-sum controller-stopper game.
The authors construct an optimal stopping time and show that the corresponding game has a value.
The upper Snell envelope of the reward process is a supermartingale with respect to an appropriately defined nonlinear expectation.
The upper Snell envelope is further an E-martingale up to the first time it meets the reward process.
The proof of the main result involves overcoming technical challenges due to the lack of a dominated convergence theorem and a measurable selection theorem.
The paper makes assumptions on the regularity of the reward process, the adaptedness and weak stability under pasting of the probability class, and the integrability of the shifted reward process.
The weak stability under pasting assumption is crucial for the dynamic programming result to hold.
The paper provides an example of path-dependent SDEs with controls that satisfies all the assumptions made in the paper.

The paper extends the results in the literature by considering a more general setting where the set of probabilities contain mutually singular probabilities and the controller can influence both the drift and the volatility.
The paper uses a global approach rather than a local approach, starting with a dynamic programming principle and carefully constructing approximating stopping times.
The first time the upper Snell envelope meets the reward process is shown to be the optimal stopping time for the robust optimal stopping problem.
The paper establishes a connection between the nonlinear expectation and the upper Snell envelope, which plays a crucial role in the main result.

The paper's technical setup closely follows that of Ekren, Touzi, and Zhang (2014), which analyzed a control problem with discretionary stopping in a non-Markovian framework with mutually singular probability priors.
